environment_note: Cattle turn grass from rangelands into food, but methane stays high because rumen microbes ferment fiber.
Concentrate feeding can raise output, but it also depends on cropland and purchased inputs.
Sheep do well on marginal pastures and mixed grazing systems.
Grain can improve growth, but sheep remain valuable where crops are difficult.
Goats browse shrubs and dry landscapes that support fewer other livestock.
Supplemental grain boosts production, but goats still shine in arid mixed systems.
Pigs can scavenge or graze lightly, but they do not use rough forage efficiently.
Pigs are efficient grain converters with low methane relative to ruminants.
